intervals.label: Yemilab construction
intervals.note: End: September 2022, the completion date given in the abstract (the conclusion of the same paper says October 2022 and an IBS slide deck gives a completion ceremony on 5 October 2022).
intervals.quote: construction of the Yemilab began in September 2017

intervals.label: interior fit-out for experiments
intervals.note: Atlas interpretation: between the finished tunnels (September 2022) and the start of experiment relocation (September 2023) the paper describes interior enhancements in 2023.
intervals.quote: With the completion of the fundamental structure of Yemilab, interior enhancements took place in 2023

intervals.label: operating; experiments relocated from Y2L
intervals.note: Start = beginning of the relocation of experiments from Yangyang (September 2023). COSINE-100U physics data taking began at Yemilab in September 2025 (arXiv:2608.11678); AMoRE-II was still 'upcoming' in July 2026 (arXiv:2607.08039).
intervals.quote: Starting in September 2023, the relocation of various facilities from Yangyang to Yemilab began.

website.note: No dedicated Yemilab website was found; this is the operating centre's page (written during construction, about 2018).
website.quote: The new underground facility, called as Yemilab, will have 1000 m thick overburden and 3000 m2 size experimental area.

name: Yemilab
notes: Yemilab was also proposed as host of non-dark-matter projects (large liquid-scintillator detector in the LSC pit, IsoDAR); those belong to the neutrino stream and are not recorded here.
Y2L slide deck of 2023: '2022.10.05 The construction completion ceremony' and '2023.08 - 2024.09 Y2L relocation to Yemilab'.

operator_text.note: Authors of the construction paper are at IBS CUP; a 2026 COSINE-100U paper lists an author at the 'Center for Yemilab Operation, Institute for Basic Science'. The mine is operated by SM Handuk Iron Mine Co., Ltd (Front. Phys. Sec. 2).
operator_text.quote: The Center for Underground Physics of the Institute for Basic Science (IBS) in Korea has been planning the construction of a deep underground laboratory since 2013
operator_text.value: Institute for Basic Science (IBS), Korea (Center for Underground Physics / Center for Yemilab Operation), inside the Handuk iron mine of SM Handuk Iron Mine Co., Ltd.

summary.plain: A deep underground laboratory about 1,000 metres below Mount Yemi in Jeongseon, South Korea, built inside an active iron mine and completed in 2022. It succeeds the Yangyang laboratory and hosts the upgraded COSINE-100U dark-matter detector and the AMoRE-II double-beta-decay experiment now being installed.
summary.technical: Yemilab: ~1,000 m overburden (about 2,500 m.w.e.) at the end of a 782 m access tunnel (12% slope) from the bottom of the Handuk mine's second shaft; limestone host rock; 17 experimental rooms including the AMoRE Hall (21 x 21 x 16 m, floor at 1,029 m depth) and the LSC Hall with a cylindrical pit of ~6,200 m3; preliminary muon flux 1.0e-7 /cm2/s, about four times lower than at Y2L. Construction September 2017 to September 2022; relocation from Y2L from 2023.
